games.explanation: San Diego's the shinier name, but Casey Mize is exactly the kind of contact-suppression illusion that a hot Cincinnati ballpark eats alive. Mize gets by on soft edges rather than swing-and-miss, and his xwOBA against righties climbs north of .310 once you strip away the sequencing luck. Elly De La Cruz has been a different hitter against right-handers this year, and Sal Stewart's barrel rate in his cameo suggests the Reds have another bat that doesn't care who's on the mound. In a park where the ball carries and a simulation that has this as a coin flip, +140 on the wrong favorite is the whole point.

Eury Perez still gets treated like a phenom on the price screen, but his contact-quality numbers tell a different story than his strikeout rate does. Right-handed bats are squaring him up at will, which is bad news when Kansas City runs Witt, Perez and a Jensen who has been absolutely mashing righties in his brief look up top. Cameron isn't a name-brand arm, but he's been the quieter and stingier pitcher of the two all season, and the Marlins order behind Hernandez thins out in a hurry. Getting a better team at a pick'em price is the whole ballgame, and -105 is a gift the market rarely leaves sitting out.

Nobody wants to touch the Cardinals in Los Angeles against Yamamoto, and that is exactly why the number got fat enough to matter. Yamamoto has been terrific, but he's been noticeably more mortal against righties, and St. Louis happens to run Herrera and Burleson at the top of a lineup that does its damage from that side. Add a park that plays down for runs but up for the one swing that flips a game, and the path to a Cardinals cover is cleaner than a 30% implied price suggests. The model has this closer to a coin flip than a coronation, and +215 on a live dog is the entire argument.

Griffin Jax is a strikeout monster against righties and a coin flip against lefties, which is a problem when the Mets can run Soto and a lefty-leaning stack through the middle innings. Hagenman is nobody's idea of an ace, but the projected margin here is half a run, not the blowout the moneyline implies.
